newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign minister leaves for Moscow.
newsitem.headline: China foreign minister leaves for Moscow.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen left for Moscow on Monday to pave the way for a visit to the Russian capital next month by President Jiang Zemin, Russian diplomats said.
Jiang is expected to sign a long-awaited accord on troop reductions along the once-tense Chinese border with Russia as well as with the Central Asian states of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.
The late April summit is also likely to review the future direction of improving Sino-Russian ties, which the two sides have described as a strategic partnership.
China and the former Soviet Union clashed along their border in the 1960s at the height of their rivalry for the leadership of the world communist movement.
Relations have improved dramatically since a 1989 visit to Beijing by Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.
Ties have improved further following the collapse of the Soviet Union and as Moscow seeks to counterbalance a planned expansion of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
Chinese officials gave no details of Qian's schedule, but Russian diplomats said other aspects of the Sino-Russian relationship, such as trade, might be discussed.
Russian officials in Beijing have said that Moscow wanted economic ties to mirror progress on the political front.
Among the projects the two nations have been discussing is a pipeline to bring Siberian oil and natural gas to China as well as Chinese purchases of Russian nuclear power technology.
Qian is also expected to discuss plans for Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to visit China in May, diplomats said.
